correctness.rationale: One position cannot cover both letters. For k=2, both positions must be interior to cover all four digrams; their incident digram sets force exactly the listed two context pairings, whose center letters differ. For k=3, covering six triples with two positions forces both centers to have three distinct incident triples. The even/odd substitution images of the six triples give the exhaustive twelve length-five contexts. The independent local check found eight pairs covering the triples: four have one letter and three digrams, two have two letters and three digrams, and exactly two have two letters and four digrams. The two-letter image boundaries give the stated four digram recurrences; their base at t_2 = 0110 and substitution induction give the even/odd count table. Each relevant triple comes from a unique pair and parity, and each relevant length-five context comes from a unique triple and parity; multiplying the two disjoint context pair contributions gives the exact unordered counts. The base cases t_3 and t_4 already contain the required contexts. An independent replay using binary digit parity and direct incident-substring sets matched the context pairs and counts through order 9; it corroborates, not replaces, the all-order argument.
residual_risks: The proof applies only to the indicated finite prefixes and length cutoffs; it makes no k≥4 claim.

value.rationale: Exact enumeration of the optimizing position sets for two natural short-factor cutoffs reveals quadratic growth, in contrast to the eventual constant unrestricted count. Cutting off at length three retains asymptotically one quarter of the length-two optima, and the exhaustive local characterization explains which pairs survive. The solution provides counts and exact witnesses rather than only a complexity bound or small-instance table.
residual_risks: The value rests on the exact two spectra and the k=3 structure, not on the overlapping k=2 local test or any asserted extension to other cutoffs.
